title: Burst mitigation leaky priority gate for Dedicated fleets
creator: Asha Mehta
description: Problem: Dedicated fleets occasionally receive short-duration traffic spikes (traffic bursts) that cause transient overloads, missed throughput commitments, and cascading latency increases. Current guarding mechanisms either drop too aggressively or allow long tail queueing that violates SLOs for premium customers. Goal: implement a lightweight admission layer that smooths bursts, preserves throughput guarantees for committed customers, and enables graceful degradation (soft-reject -> downgrade -> enqueue) while feeding signals to the autoscaler and the routing layer.
design_summary: We propose a leaky priority gate (LPG) per-fleet that combines multi-class token accounting, short-duration request reservoirs, and a closed-loop feedback signal to the autoscaler. Core components: 1) Per-customer weighted token credits representing reserved throughput; credits refill continuously and are consumed at request admission time. 2) Short-lived leaky reservoirs (time-bounded queues) that buffer excess low-priority traffic for up to a configurable window (e.g., 250ms - 2s). 3) Soft-decision path: when both tokens and reservoir are exhausted, LPG issues ordered fallbacks: a) return a controlled 429 with informative headers for clients to retry, b) route to lower-cost model variant (if configured), or c) drop requests for non-critical labels. 4) Feedback loop: LPG exports aggregated short-window metrics (token utilization, reservoir fill, rejects) and a binary backpressure flag to the autoscaler so it can scale up proactively during sustained bursts, and scale down conservatively after drain windows. 5) Policy primitives exposed in fleet config: minimum reserved RPS, burst_headroom_ms, eviction_policy (LRU/oldest/label-priority), degrade_rules (model_fallback, cost_center_fallback, hard_reject).
acceptance_criteria: LPG deploys in canary fleet and does not increase 99th percentile latency for P0 customers by >5% under baseline traffic
During a synthetic 5x burst (1 minute) LPG maintains reserved RPS for customers with reservations and limits P3 customers to configured throttles with <2% unexpected success rate
Autoscaler receives backpressure flag and triggers scale-up within configured policy window (validated in staging)
Dashboards for token utilization, reservoir occupancy, and fallback rates are live in the console and have alert triggers for sustained rejects
updates: 2026-02-20: RFC created and reviewed with infra and product. Initial design captured in confluence (link below).

2026-02-25: Simulated burst models against traffic traces from three customers; LPG parameters (reservoir_ms=500, token_refill=continuous) were tuned to preserve reserved throughput while reducing peak drop-rate by ~62% compared to baseline tokenbucket-only approach.
2026-03-02: Engineering spike: implemented prototype gateway filter and local reservoir with feature flag. Load tests in the perf lab show modest CPU overhead (~4%) at 95th percentile throughput.
2026-03-06: Security review triage — no secrets in LPG, but request headers used for routing must be audited. Added audit task to Private deployment checklist.
2026-03-10: Integration test pipeline added; canary rollout plan drafted. Next: extend autoscaler signal contract and coordinate with release manager for runtime-1.24 rollout.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Reservoiring can increase tail latency for some clients. Mitigation: strict per-class reservoirs and short max buffering windows plus telemetry to detect regressions.
Risk: Priority inversion where many small reserved customers starve a larger committed customer. Mitigation: implement weighted tokens with minimum allocation and cross-customer fairness window.
Risk: Autoscaler thrash if feedback noisy. Mitigation: use aggregated short-window flag + smoothed rate and hysteresis in autoscaler policies.
